blocks.text: Laura spat.

The small orange shot cut through the taut joining rope and scorched the nearest wrist turns. She wrenched her hands apart, tearing the blackened fibers. Another quick shot burned the rope across her coat. She dragged an arm free, shrugged out of the loosened loops and scrambled up.
Daniel glanced over his shoulder, then bent back to the meters.
blocks.alt: Laura rises beside the rooftop vent, her hands free and severed rope discarded at her boots.

blocks.text: Laura took one step toward the collector. Inside the glass, Flaming Head lifted his eyes to hers.
“Keep clear of the machine, Laura. It’s too dangerous.”
His warning reached her mind alone. Daniel and Luke heard nothing.
She looked at the switch beneath Daniel’s hand. She could still go toward it.
Instead, she stepped back.
“You’ll have to work on it,” she said.
She turned toward the stairhouse. His eyes followed her through the glass.
blocks.alt: Laura turns toward the stairs, choosing to leave the weakened Flaming Head trapped inside the active collector.

blocks.text: Behind her, the hum climbed to a thin, unsteady whine.
Luke drifted nearer the western panel. Both needles had reached the ends of their scales. Orange light crowded the cylinder until he could barely see the little face inside.
“It’s full,” he said.
Daniel kept his hand on the knob. “A little more.”
A bright line opened in the glass.
“Uncle—”
Daniel reached for the switch.
The collector exploded.
White light burst from the western housing. The blast caught Luke beside the meters and hurled him backward across the clear strip.
blocks.alt: The overloaded collector bursts at its western controls, throwing Luke backward without his jaws touching the machine; sparks catch Daniel’s coat hem.

blocks.text: He struck the bricked-up warehouse window. Mortar burst around his head, and he vanished through the opening in a cloud of dust.
Laura ducked behind the stairhouse corner. Hot fragments rattled against the brick.
Daniel staggered away from the panel. A burning scrap had caught the loose hem of his lab coat. The cloth flared.
He recoiled, tore the coat off and stamped at it, backing toward the stairhouse.
blocks.alt: Daniel holds his burning lab coat away from his body after sparks from the collector explosion ignite its lower hem.

blocks.text: The glass split between the copper coils. Both needles fell, and the whine stopped.
A small orange flame escaped through the brass mouth and drifted low above the roof.
Daniel left the smoking coat and hurried to the broken window. Luke lay motionless among the bricks on the warehouse floor.
blocks.alt: Luke’s iron-jawed head breaks through the warehouse’s bricked-up window after the collector explosion.

blocks.text: Flaming Head rose unsteadily beside the ruined cylinder. His crest barely cleared his brow.
Laura stood in the stairhouse doorway. For a moment he looked toward her.
She pulled her coat closer and stayed where she was.
He turned away. The little light cleared the northern parapet and sank beyond it.
Daniel called Luke’s name into the warehouse. There was no answer.
Behind the stairhouse, Laura wiped dust from her mouth. The familiar heat in her throat had dwindled.
She found a steel offcut lying flat on the bare gravel, clear of anything that could burn. A small shot should have pierced it.
She spat.
The orange streak struck, hissed and faded. No hole opened.
Laura crouched beside the steel. There was only a shallow scorched dimple.
blocks.alt: Alone behind the stairhouse, Laura examines the shallow scorch her weakened plasma has left on a steel offcut.

blocks.text: She tried once more. The second mark was scarcely deeper.
“Lava Lips?” Daniel called.
She pushed the steel beneath a broken pallet with her boot.
He came around the corner in his gray shirt, his tie hanging crookedly. “Your power. Any trouble?”
Laura straightened. “Same as before.”
His glasses flashed as he looked at her. “Stay here. I need to see to Luke.”
She waited until he had gone, then rubbed the cold tips of her gloves together. He was not going to look at her the way he looked at his broken machine.
